_comment: Lectern's filter. A posting is KEPT if any role_title word appears in its title, or if three or more topic_text words appear in its body. flex_text never causes a keep — it only annotates a kept record, because 'part-time' on its own has nothing to do with teaching. Every kept record records which words matched and where, so a reader can apply this file by hand to one posting and get the same answer. v0.2.0 (2026-09-26): added the alternative titles these roles are posted under — Developer/Designer/Creator Advocate, Design or Product Evangelist, Community Engineer, Community Architect, Product Education Manager, Technical Content Engineer, Developer Experience, DevRel, Technical Writer. Several are broad on purpose and the run report measures what noise they added. v0.2.1 (2026-09-26, same day): REMOVED 'developer experience' and 'advocacy' after measuring them. 'developer experience' fired on 11 postings and 10 were backend or platform software-engineering jobs (Anthropic, Figma, Stripe x2, GitLab, OpenAI x2, Notion, Replit, Canva) — the phrase names an engineering discipline, not an advocacy role. 'advocacy' fired once, on a customer-marketing programme. Kept: 'devrel', which found Vercel's DevRel Engineer. This is what P3 is for — the filter is a file, so a word that turns out to be noise gets cut and the cut is recorded. v0.3.0 (2026-09-26): Professor Bear refined the target — any job that DEVELOPS MATERIALS, whether to sell into universities, to teach the public, or to train the company's own people. Anthropic's 'Technical Documentation and Content Engineer, Claude Docs' is the model. Measured every candidate word against all 3,446 titles before adding: 11 of them appear in ZERO titles today and so cannot add noise; 'creator', 'documentation', and 'content engineer' each appear in exactly one title and it is the right one. 'learning experiences' found Replit's LEARNING EXPERIENCES CREATOR, a bullseye that v0.2.1 missed because it only had 'learning designer'. REJECTED as measured noise: bare 'learning' (42 titles, almost all Machine/Reinforcement Learning) and 'content strategy' (3 titles, all regional SEO marketing). v0.6.0 (2026-10-26): TWO GATES that apply after the keywords. Professor Bear, looking at a 'K12 Education Account Manager, South Korea (12 months contract), Seoul' from a design-software company: 'keep it to English-speaking countries? Unless it's France or Italy. Or Brazil? Or Portugal? And no K-12.' A posting the keywords would keep is now rejected, with its reason, if (1) location_rule: its place names no allowed country (the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Ireland, France, Italy, Brazil, Portugal), or (2) k12_rule: its TITLE says K-12. Both are data at the end of this file and collect.py only reads them. The gates never touch a posting the keywords reject, so every old reject keeps its old reason. The numbers behind each choice are in measured_before_adding; the choices that are Professor Bear's to change are named in the _comment of each rule.

ignore_words_by_company._comment: Words that appear in (nearly) every posting on that board — company boilerplate, not a signal. Measured, not guessed. Writer, 2026-09-19: these three appeared in 51 of 51 postings and alone pushed every job over the line.

materials_rule._comment: Professor Bear, 2026-09-26: 'everything's probably named differently, but that kind of job would be something to look out for.' Titles cannot carry this family — 'documentation' is in 2 of 3,446 titles and 'technical writer' in zero — so a posting is also KEPT when its BODY says the job is to produce teaching materials FOR a named audience. Both halves are required: a make-materials phrase AND an audience. 'Maintain documentation' in a tax director's ad matches the first and not the second, which is the whole point. TIGHTENED same day after measurement: the first version kept 101 extra postings at roughly one-in-ten precision, because phrases like 'technical documentation' and 'technical content' appear in almost every engineering, support, and legal ad — every product has docs. Nine phrase groups were removed and the threshold raised to TWO verb-object phrases. The removed list is kept here because a rule that failed is evidence about the corpus, not an embarrassment. Final pass: threshold back to ONE phrase (two matched nothing in the whole corpus), and three more phrases cut. The surviving list is 23 phrases that only a teaching-materials job uses. Measured precision of the body rule after all cuts is in the run report; it is the only rule here whose precision was measured rather than assumed, because it was the only one that failed loudly enough to force it.

connector_rule._comment: Professor Bear, 2026-10-18, looking at a Senior Partner Account Manager posting for global systems integrators (correctly rejected: it is a sales role about consulting firms, not education): 'the search should look for jobs like this' for universities: a role that owns a big institutional relationship, the way Claude and Northeastern is a big account. Not a teaching job and not a teaching-materials job, so neither older rule can see it by design. Both halves required: an account-or-partnership word in the TITLE and a higher-education institution in the BODY. Measured on the 2026-10-18 corpus (3,243 postings) before adding: 495 titles carry an account or partnership word; 7 of those also name a university or higher education in the body; 5 of the 7 were already kept (Canva and OpenAI higher-education account roles, Anthropic's AI for Science partnership role) and 2 are new. Precision is NOT measured: 2 new postings is too few to say, and a person has to read them. 'customer success' was left out because it is a support title at most companies. 2026-10-18, second pass (v0.5.1), after Professor Bear read the closest-call table and confirmed that industry Enterprise Account Executive roles (retail, banking, automotive and the rest, 27 on the board) are correct rejects: 'educate them about our services' is sales boilerplate, not teaching. The fit he named is an account executive who reaches universities. Re-measured: 57 postings name a university or higher education in the body; 5 of those have a sales or partner-style title and are not kept. Four are not account roles (a solutions-marketing lead, two state-and-local-affairs leads, a public-sector operations lead) and stay out. One, a Sales Manager for nonprofits in EMEA that names higher education, is the kind of role he described, so 'sales manager', 'sales director', 'sales executive' and 'enterprise sales' were added to the title words. Only 'sales manager' matches anything today; the other three are 'zero titles today, no noise possible'. All 38 Enterprise Account Executive roles on the boards (28 at Anthropic; 'industry' ones such as retail, banking and automotive) still come out as rejects. (An earlier draft of this note said 27; that was a miscount of the Anthropic lines, corrected 2026-10-18.) 2026-10-18, third pass (v0.5.2), after Professor Bear read the reject file, found no misses, and asked that marketing, adoption and enterprise-account roles not be rejected early ('I'm okay with looking at a few more'). Re-measured on the same corpus: 992 postings have a marketing, adoption, customer-success, account, partner, sales or growth word in the title; 13 of those name a university or higher education in the body; 12 were already kept; 1 was rejected (a Solutions Marketing Lead for the public sector), and 'marketing' now keeps it. 'adoption', 'customer success', 'go-to-market' and 'gtm' match nothing new today. A weaker body half was also tried and NOT added: accepting two or more education words (education, students, schools, k-12, learners, teachers) instead of a university gave 2 extra rejects and 0 that fit (a public-health partnerships role where 'schools' means school health, and a hardware marketing role where 'students' is a consumer group).

location_rule._comment: Which countries a posting may be in. Professor Bear, 2026-10-26: English-speaking countries, plus France, Italy, Brazil and Portugal. TO CHANGE THE LIST edit allowed_countries: use a name that is a key of `countries` below. Every country the reader can recognise is already there, so adding India or Singapore is one word, nothing else. THE CHOICES THAT ARE HIS, each with the default taken and what it costs (counts: the postings the keywords alone would keep in an 84,282-posting snapshot of 2026-10-24, titles and places only: 1,056, of which this rule drops 146; on the six watched boards 58 and 8). (a) Which countries are 'English-speaking': the default is the narrow list, the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and Ireland. NOT included, with what each would bring back: India 20 postings (1 on the six boards), Singapore 22 (0), Philippines 3, Hong Kong 3, South Africa 0. (b) A location that names no country ('Remote', 'Hybrid', 'N/A', 'EMEA', 'Remote - Europe') is KEPT (if_no_country_named: keep) and the record says location.country_named is false, because a place the reader cannot read should reach a person, not vanish: 50 postings in the snapshot, 2 of 82 in the 2026-10-18 run. Set it to "reject" to drop them. (c) A posting in several places is allowed if ANY one is ('Berlin, Germany | Austin, TX' is kept; a line of only foreign places is rejected; a foreign place beside one that cannot be read is kept). (d) Puerto Rico counts as the United States; 'Georgia' alone counts as the American state. HOW A PLACE IS READ, so it can be done by hand: the line is split on the separators into places; in each place the first of these that is found decides it: a country's own name or abbreviation (names), then a state or province code after a comma, hyphen or bracket ('Athens, GA' is Georgia, USA; codes), then a city or region (places). Names that are also American towns (Lebanon, Jamaica, Holland, Berlin) sit among the places, so a state code beats them. Longer names win ('New Mexico' is not Mexico). A string two countries share goes to the allowed one: a stray posting costs less than a lost one. Words in workplace_words ('Remote', 'Hybrid') are not places. Accents are ignored ('Sao Paulo'). MEASURED: against the country codes the boards themselves report, on 37,470 postings where both the board and the reader name a country, they agree on 37,458; the 12 that differ are postings in several places (the board reports one code) and the country Georgia. KNOWN WEAK SPOTS: a foreign city with no country written and not in `places` is read as 'no country named' and kept; a list is not the world, and the audit (audit/audit_gates.py) shows the unread places so they can be added.

k12_rule._comment: No K-12 roles, in any country. Professor Bear, 2026-10-26: 'And no K-12. No.' DEFAULT (narrow): the TITLE says K-12 in any spelling (K12, K-12, K–12, K -12) or names a grade band (K-8, pre-K, kindergarten, elementary, middle, high, primary or secondary school). Measured on the titles of the 84,282-posting snapshot: 212 hits, 201 at one charter-school network (not on the watch list), 6 Instructure sales titles ending '- K12', Esri 1, Canva 2 (the K12 Education Account Manager in Seoul and its twin in Vietnam), Khan Academy 1 ('Elementary School 3 - 5'), Stripe 1 ('High School Internship'). On the six watched boards: 2. TRAPS CHECKED: 'K8' is Kubernetes (3 titles, Coupang and OneTrust), so the list says 'k-8' with a hyphen and does not match it; 'K12' is also a company's name, but the company field is not read, so a company called K12 is not a K-12 role by its name. THE BODY IS NOT READ (body_phrases is empty), which is a choice that is his: 5 of the 3,243 saved ads say K-12, 4 of them are kept, and all 4 are broad education roles that also name higher education (three OpenAI Education roles: 'higher education institutions, K-12 districts, and country-level partnerships'; a Canva Indonesia education marketing role: 'across K-12 and Higher Education'). Put "k-12" in body_phrases to drop them too. NOT CAUGHT BY THE TITLE RULE: Canva's 'District Education Advocate, South Korea' in the 2026-10-18 ad was the same job before it was retitled 'K12 Education Account Manager'; its ad says 'school system' and never 'K-12'. Only the country rule dropped it.
